clue.text: On mine, you'll get this: "A bore has a big one"

definitions.text: On mine, you'll get this: "A bore has a big one"

parts.words: On mine, you'll get this: "A bore has a big one"
parts.note: someone in tune with my thinking is on my ..., and a tidal bore is a huge wave with a long distance between crests

explanation.walkthrough: Two ideas meet in one phrase: being 'on my wavelength' means sharing my outlook, while a bore (a tidal surge up a river such as the Severn) is a wave, so it literally has a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on my wavelength' means thinking alike, and a tidal wave's crest spacing is its physical measure.

clue.text: Georgia flicked it at soldiers, being a troublemaker

indicators.note: flicked over, so the abbreviation for Georgia is flipped round

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
taken as written
taken as written
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone from Georgia flicks something at the troops and is branded a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser who stirs up unrest is a synonym for a troublemaker; 'being' links the noun to the wordplay.

clue.text: Obsessive about Homeric character in book

indicators.note: the word for obsessive goes round, surrounding the Greek letter

parts.note: anal, in the informal sense, means fussy and obsessive
NU is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character Homer would have written

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on a figure from Homer appears in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homeric character' looks like Achilles or Odysseus, but it is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly hardback such as a children's comic compilation is a kind of book.

clue.text: Looking up a little, seeking victory

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the letters bottom to top
only a little of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Searching upward, with a bit of hope, for a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes EKIN from inside 'seeking'; 'Looking up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the Greek goddess personifying victory.

clue.text: Dance on pitch before animal drops off parent

parts.note: pitch is tar, the black sticky substance
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: the parent is dropped from the end of the animal's name

parts.note: a llama is a South American pack animal
ma is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A dance takes place on the field before an animal drops its rider's parent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops off' removes MA from LLAMA, leaving LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance.

clue.text: Iris pursues a butterfly seen flying on some beaches

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the iris follows the butterfly

parts.note: a blue is a kind of small butterfly
flag is another name for the iris plant

explanation.surface: An iris flower chases a butterfly flitting along the seashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blue Flag is an award for clean beaches, flown on a flagpole there.

clue.text: Calendar guy?

parts.note: the calendar introduced by Caesar bears a man's name, and that name is also a boy's first name

explanation.walkthrough: The calendar Julius Caesar introduced is named after him, and the same word is an ordinary man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Roman calendar takes its name from Julius, and a man may be called by that name today.

clue.text: Great match — second half on top

indicators.note: in a down clue the latter half of the word is moved up above the first half

parts.note: a game is a match

explanation.surface: A great football match where the second half outshines the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half on top' moves ME before GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang meaning great or tremendous.

clue.text: Man enters dock, heading off for the country

indicators.note: the man goes inside the dock word
the first letter of the dock word is removed

parts.note: a marina is a dock for boats
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man walks into a dock and sets off for another land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like part of the surface story but supplies the gentleman; 'heading off' drops the first letter of the dock word.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, so it names a country.

clue.text: Contemptible person steals one from a woman

indicators.note: steals means takes away, so the numeral is lifted out of the name

parts.note: Louise is a woman's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A despicable man pinches something from a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steals' takes I out of LOUISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a louse is an insult for a mean, despicable person.

clue.text: Trespass in exchange for mould

indicators.note: one thing is given for another, a swap of letters within the word

parts.note: to intrude is to trespass
taken as written
ex is an abbreviation for exchange

explanation.surface: Someone trespasses in return for something to shape.
explanation.walkthrough: IN at the start of INTRUDE is swapped for EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to shape a material by forcing it through a die, a way of moulding it.

clue.text: The place to give us capitalisation?

definitions.text: The place to give us capitalisation?

parts.words: The place to give us capitalisation?
parts.note: written with capitals, the little word us becomes the initials of the United States

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalise 'us' and you get US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by the continent's name, so the country is the place in question.

clue.text: "Praise first wife", many reflected

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, such as a first wife

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word backwards

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A man praises his first wife, and many people think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns LOT into TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Stroke uncle with a ruptured spleen

parts.note: to pet is to stroke

indicators.note: ruptured means burst apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strokes an uncle who has suffered a burst spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruptured' rearranges UNCLE and A into ULANCE. 'spleen' looks like the organ, but here it means bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen, in its old sense, is bad temper or peevishness.

clue.text: Tirades delivered after man snaps

indicators.note: the man comes first and the snaps after him

parts.note: Philip is a man's name
pics are photographs, snaps

explanation.surface: Angry rants follow after a man takes photos.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon.
explanation.definitionFit: Philippics are bitter denunciations spoken against someone, so they are tirades given aloud.

clue.text: American state where dollars 'ave circulated since 2001

indicators.note: circulated means moved around, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Latin American country where US dollars have been the currency since 2001.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' mixes DOLLARS and AVE; El Salvador did adopt the US dollar in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is a sovereign state in Central America.

clue.text: The King's film shows soldiers holding hands, again and again

annotationWithheld.why: The King's film shows soldiers holding hands, again and again (5,5,5): GIS round RL makes GIRLS, and 'again and again' needs it three times; rep() gives only two copies, and a third needs 'soldiers', 'hands' and 'holding' doing two jobs, which the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: The King's film shows soldiers holding hands, again and again

clue.text: Wraps up old woman in smalls

indicators.note: the old woman goes inside the smalls

parts.note: S is small, so two smalls give two of that letter
old woman is slang for mother

explanation.surface: Someone wraps an old woman up in underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' looks like underwear (British slang), but it is S plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up completely, to wrap it.

clue.text: Groundsman extremely relieved, falling for a woman

indicators.note: falling means tumbling about, so the letters are rearranged
relieved of its extremes, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A groundsman, greatly relieved, falls for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely relieved' trims GROUNDSMAN to ROUNDSMA; 'falling' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosamund is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Music maker is hurt tossing a coin

parts.note: to harm is to hurt

indicators.note: a coin toss throws it about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A musical instrument gets damaged when someone flips a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' rearranges A and COIN into ONICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is an instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Tree south of Reading, for example, is looking more healthy

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means below, so the tree comes after

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs of basic education
an osier is a willow tree

explanation.surface: A tree in the south of the town of Reading looks healthier.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English town, but here it is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: A rosier complexion is pinker and healthier-looking.

clue.text: Order back ruler ceding half an Arabian city

indicators.note: back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: the ruler gives up half of his title, its last three letters

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: An Arabian ruler orders a retreat while giving up half his lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OM into MO; 'ceding half' cuts SULTAN to SUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosul is a city in northern Iraq, in the Arab world.

clue.text: Rising before noon, 10s reveal hostility

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a.m. means before noon
the answer to 10 across in the plural, insects that infest hair

explanation.surface: Getting up before midday reveals ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns AM into MA. '10s' points to the answer to 10 across, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, the wish to harm someone.

clue.text: Thorny fruit cut nurses tights, top to bottom

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the cut holds the other piece

parts.note: a rip is a tear or cut

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end

parts.note: hose is hosiery such as tights

explanation.surface: A nurse cuts her tights on a thorny bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tights' is hosiery; 'top to bottom' moves its first letter to the end before the cut wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose hip is the fruit of the rose, a thorny plant.

clue.text: Stone put in ground, the odd bits moving

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions, first and third, move around and swap places

parts.note: to bury is to put in the ground

explanation.surface: A stone gets buried, with odd things moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the odd bits moving' swaps B and R, the first and third letters of BURY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: Puzzle book — turn cover first

indicators.note: the turned cover goes before the book
to turn something over is to reverse it

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A puzzle book where you turn the cover first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes DIL from LID.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a problem with no easy answer, a puzzle.

clue.text: Learned judge gave millions to gain power, ultimately

indicators.note: gave means gave up, so a letter is surrendered
something is gained in exchange for what was given up

parts.note: to deem is to judge
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A learned judge gave away millions to win power in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' says the swap is at the end: DEEM gives up its last-letter M for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean profound, showing great learning.

clue.text: Dim headlights when animal crosses

indicators.note: the animal goes across, spanning the letter

parts.note: a bear is an animal
the head of lights, its first letter

explanation.surface: Headlights grow dim as an animal crosses the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means dim or blurred, as bleary eyes are.

clue.text: Cut short street party building to a climax

indicators.note: cut short means losing its final letter

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A street party is cut short just as it builds to its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' removes T from CRESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness, building to a peak.
